articles.title: Sophie Cunningham’s NSFW gesture on court goes viral amid Indiana Fever’s plea for stunning WNBA award
articles.summary: International Sports News: Sophie Cunningham is again at the center of a viral moment. A casual pregame video from the Indiana Fever’s home arena caught the veteran guard in a p.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham is again at the center of a viral moment. A casual pregame video from the Indiana Fever’s home arena caught the veteran guard in a playful exchange with the person filming, with a brief wardrobe slip quickly drawing attention online. Cunningham appeared unfazed, turning back toward the camera with a wide smile and a playful gesture. The lighthearted clip soon took on a life of its own, adding another memorable moment to a season in which Cunningham has given Fever fans plenty to talk about.The viral scene surfaced as Cunningham is building a much more serious case for one of the WNBA’s individual awards. Her second season in Indiana has been a major turnaround after an injury ended her first campaign with the Fever. Now, she has become an important piece of one of the league’s strongest offenses, providing efficient outside shooting alongside Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston.Sophie Cunningham makes NSFW gesture on courtSophie Cunningham’s viral moment came before an Indiana Fever game, when she was captured wearing a red Fever sweatshirt and dark pants while moving around the team’s home arena.For a brief moment, the back of her pants sat low enough for a small section of white fabric underneath to show. Cunningham quickly turned toward the camera, smiled broadly and pointed a finger at the person filming. Her pink nail polish was visible as she made the playful gesture.The original post described the scene simply as “Sophie Cunningham before the game,” presenting it as a funny pregame interaction rather than a formal interview or basketball highlight. Cunningham has earned quite the fame.Indiana Fever endorse Sophie Cunningham for 6th Player of the YearCunningham’s biggest argument for Sixth Player of the Year has come through her production. After missing much of her first season with Indiana because of a season-ending injury, the veteran guard has returned with a much larger role in her second year.Through 38 games, Cunningham is averaging 8.4 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists while shooting 47.6% from the field. Her 44.1% shooting from 3-point range has been especially impressive. The mark ranks fourth in the WNBA, behind Kelsey Mitchell, New York Liberty guard Leonie Fiebich and Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier.Cunningham has also knocked down 63 3-pointers this season, giving Indiana another dependable scoring threat around its core.The Fever made their support for her award bid clear on Thursday.“She gives us the juice when she comes in off the bench.” 🧃 “Sophie Cunningham for 6th Player of the Year 🔥,” the team posted.Cunningham scored a season-high 24 points against the Toronto Tempo on June 16, going 6-for-7 from 3-point range. The six made 3-pointers matched her career high.She later produced another six 3-pointers while scoring 20 points in Indiana’s 109-75 win over the Las Vegas Aces. Her next opportunity comes Friday, when the Fever host the Sun. Tipoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on ION.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Praggnanandhaa’s golden summer: From Norway Chess glory to GCT crown
articles.summary: Chess News: Until this summer, no Indian had won the elite Norway Chess title. There was no Indian name alongside the Grand Chess Tour finale either. R Praggnanan.
articles.body: Until this summer, no Indian had won the elite Norway Chess title. There was no Indian name alongside the Grand Chess Tour finale either. R Praggnanandhaa, that shy and super-sharp boy from Chennai, a Viswanathan Anand mentee like many from the city, now has both crowns to call his own.Late on Thursday, Praggnanandhaa, the world No. 12, claimed the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) title, beating Fabiano Caruana 15-13 in St Louis, US, considered the new Linares in chess circles, and pocketed $200,000 in prize money. Praggnanandhaa thus became the first Indian and only the seventh player in the tournament’s 11-year history to achieve the feat.It won’t be an exaggeration to call him the ‘unofficial’ Total Chess world champion ahead of the tournament’s inauguration next year and the pilot project later this year in Budapest.The 21-year-old has chosen to play next month’s Olympiad over the lucrative Global Chess League in Bengaluru. That decision has worked out very well for him because he achieved a major success well in time for the Olympiad, where India will try to defend their maiden team gold medal in three weeks’ time.The positive tidings for Indian chess don’t seem to end. The crop is fearless and the results are relentless, more importantly, at the ‘above Elo 2600’ level and not just below it or in the many online versions of the sport.Earlier this year, Praggnanandhaa had done the unthinkable by beating world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen twice in classical games at Norway Chess, a feat that included an unprecedented sequence of four straight classical wins at the end of the tournament in Oslo.If the Indian chess sun was shining brightly then, it has now just extended its rays to a new region.Praggnanandhaa has shown year-round consistency by topping the GCT table, with only the top four making it to the finale. And then, despite losing the first classical game of the final to Caruana in the title clash and messing up a probable equaliser in the second classical game, worth six points, he still displayed admirable mental strength.Praggnanandhaa won both rapid games, worth four points each, to take the lead over the highly regarded Caruana before drawing the four-game blitz section 4-4, with one win for either player. He had beaten German super talent Vincent Keymer in the semifinals.While this may be subjective, and the chess world has its favourites, experts consider Praggnanandhaa a more well-rounded Indian player than world champion Gukesh and former Elo 2800 member Arjun Erigaisi, partly due to his technical prowess and more universal style of play.That is why his failed campaigns at the 2024 and 2026 Candidates, and the manner in which he imploded, were particularly disheartening for Indian fans.Praggnanandhaa’s St Louis schedule was gruelling. He played 27 rapid and blitz games, then nine classical games, and another 16 games in the semifinals and finals of the Tour.Now, he can rest with a sense of achievement, a high like no other.When his sister Vaishali was not doing too well at the Classical Cairns Cup for women, being played concurrently at the same venue, Praggnanandhaa was plotting his own grand prize. The roles were reversed at the Cyprus Candidates earlier this year when Vaishali won the women’s title and Praggnanandhaa finished seventh in the eight-player field.Not that Praggnanandhaa hadn’t proved himself before at the elite level. He burst into the limelight by reaching the 2023 World Cup final in Baku, the birthplace of the great Garry Kasparov, in Azerbaijan, and has now stamped his authority on the GCT Tour, which has been the brainchild of the Russian.In between his knockout World Cup run and the Norway title, he had several high points. But those came largely in the classical section, with triumphs at Wijk aan Zee, the GCT Romania leg and the UzChess Cup in 2025, all in classical chess.World championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov had humbled Praggnanandhaa twice at the Cyprus Candidates. The Indian avenged those defeats at the Sinquefield Cup, where he finished joint first.Keymer defeated Praggnanandhaa at Sinquefield before getting knocked out by the Indian’s cerebral powers in the semifinals of the Tour Finale.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Grand Chess Tour: ‘Praggnanandhaa refused to settle for second place’
articles.summary: Chess News: CHENNAI: It was the middle of the night in India when golden boy R Praggnanandhaa made history in St Louis, USA. As the 21-year-old became the first I.
articles.body: CHENNAI: It was the middle of the night in India when golden boy R Praggnanandhaa made history in St Louis, USA. As the 21-year-old became the first Indian to win the Grand Chess Tour (GCT), his long-time coach RB Ramesh and second, GM Vaibhav Suri, were wide awake back home.For the two men, sleep had been the last thing on their minds over the past month as they kept a close watch on Pragg’s campaign in St Louis. After his sensational triumph, Pragg was quick to acknowledge the hours they had put in behind the scenes.“A special appreciation to my trainers, Ramesh sir and Vaibhav. Especially Vaibhav, he compromised his sleep schedule for me. Back home, he was chatting with me despite the time difference. Huge credit to him. He was online throughout… it’s like 3 or 4 am back home,” Pragg said after scripting a remarkable comeback.Pragg overturned a six-point deficit on the final day to beat Fabiano Caruana 15-13. He had been in difficult positions several times during the tournament, but Suri felt it was Pragg’s relentless drive and refusal to give up that helped him rise above them — and, in turn, made the trainer’s job easier.“Six points against a player like Fabiano is not the ideal situation to be in. But the best thing about Pragg is that he has a very strong character. It’s very easy to feel, in a situation like that, when you have very slim chances, ‘Maybe it’s not my tournament’, ‘It’s not my day’, ‘I can let this go.’ He did not feel any of that at all.“I could sense it from the way we were communicating, discussing game strategy, match strategy and opening prep. It’s much easier for me and the others around him to put in that effort when you know the person you’re helping is extremely driven and really wants this. Obviously, at this stage, you don’t want to be satisfied with second place or simply being a GCT finalist,” Suri, beaming with pride, told TOI from New Delhi.That mindset has been central to Pragg’s evolution as a player. No longer the precocious kid who announced himself on the world stage, he has grown into a more complete player — one who can hold his own across all three formats. His results this year have been telling.After a disappointing outing at the Candidates in April, Pragg won Norway Chess, followed it up with the Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz title, finished runner-up at the Sinquefield Cup and now has the GCT crown.Ramesh, who has guided Pragg since he was a wide-eyed child, feels his protege is now playing with greater confidence, particularly in shorter time controls, which have not always been his strongest suit.“Winning such big events always gives tremendous confidence,” Ramesh told TOI. “I think that is very important. Being consistent across all three formats is not easy. If they do well in one format, they struggle in another. But he has done well in all three. I hope this is just the beginning because he has to do this consistently across all four formats. That won’t be easy because adapting to different time controls is not easy.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Maryland volleyball takes down Howard, 3-0, in season opener
articles.summary: The Terps stormed into the district with relentless offense to lay the groundwork for their 2026 campaign.
articles.body:
It wasn't always smooth sailing, but Maryland women's volleyball got it done in its season opener.

Despite brief charges from Howard, the Terps rarely wavered and cruise to a three-set victory in the nation's capital.

Howard set the tone early and took the lead for most of the tightly-contested first set.

Alexys James sparked the Bison offensively, recording three kills in the opening points as the teams traded scores early. This firepower drove Howard to build its largest lead of the set, 17-12, after a service ace from Sydnei Jones forced Maryland to call a timeout.

The Terps came out of the timeout fierce, quickly leveling the game at 18 points apiece. Hughes' timeout was perfectly executed to help his team turn things around. The five-point deficit looked largely self-inflicted at the moment — there were multiple instances of miscommunication and avoidable errors that cost the Terps points. Maryland took its first lead of the game, 20-19.

The two teams continued to trade points, but the Terps ultimately held on to complete the comeback, taking the opening set 25-23 after anattacking error from Howard.

Maryland brought the momentum into the second set, quickly taking control after a close start. The Terps began to create separation behind points from Sydney Bryant and Haley Melby, while Howard struggled to create offense.

After narrowly winning the opening set, Maryland completely took over. The effort was heavily assisted by the Terps' balanced offense, which allowed for more contributors to shine as opposed to relying on a single point scorer.

Despite a timeout from the Bison, the Terps did not take their foot off the gas. The break only added fuel to the fire, as Maryland extended their lead to their largest of the match, 12 points, before closing out the set in 25-14 fashion.

Ava Brown showed why the Maryland freshman class was one to watch, contributing several key kills as the Terps continued to overwhelm Howard's defense. Brown was joined by supporting offensive performances from Bryant, Melby, and Duru Gökçen.

Howard pushed Maryland harder in the final set, taking a17-16 at one point late in the set. Despite the early lead Maryland had, Howard evened out the contest with crucial kills coupled with defensive errors from the Terps. Eventually, though, Maryland was able to break away and pull off the sweep in the final five points of the match.

Sara Toth was the key performer for Maryland Friday. In her Maryland debut, the Georgia Tech transfer recorded 46 assists and two kills. Maryland hit 0.434 as a team, a strong indication that Toth was effective in distributing the offense and getting multiple hitters involved.

The Terps will look to keep this energy up going into the Big Ten-SEC Challenge on Tuesday in Nashville.

Maryland's offense was clicking. The Terps finished the night on top thanks to a well-rounded attack. Brown led the way with 17 kills, while Melby added 12 and Bryant added nine.

The freshmen made an immediate impact. Brown quickly established her presence in Maryland's offense in her first match with the program. Raina Chwialkowski led the Terps with 10 digs.

The Terps showed resilience when tested. Maryland could've easily dropped the first set after falling behind 17-12. Instead, they battled back to win it, 25-23. Howard challenged the Terps again in the third set, but Maryland resisted to complete the sweep.

articles.title: 'Every time you play Rangers, it is a difficult game' - Robinson
articles.summary: Aberdeen head coach Stephen Robinson says his side will need to be at the top of their game to beat Rangers at Pittodrie on Sunday, despite the visitors' dif...
articles.body:
Aberdeen head coach Stephen Robinson says his side will need to be at the top of their game to beat Rangers at Pittodrie on Sunday, despite the visitors' difficult start to the season.

Derek McInnes and his team are already under pressure amid a poor run of performances that continued in the Czech Republic on Thursday night, when they were knocked out of the Conference League by Jablonec.

"We have to focus on ourselves first and foremost and what we bring to the game," Robinson said

"We have to bring the best version of ourselves. Every time you play Rangers, it is a difficult game.

"It doesn't matter what stage of the season it is and where they are in terms of results, you play Rangers, you have to be on top of your game to win the game."

Aberdeen have enjoyed a solid start to the season, losing just one of their seven games, and should be pretty fresh after last weekend's encounter with Motherwell was postponed because of the Steelmen's European commitments.

"I am not sure it is an advantage," Robinson insisted. "Players want to keep playing football and momentum all the time.

"We had a game last week, a practice game as well, so we have tried to keep the momentum going.

"We come into it positive after a really good week's training and I don't think it is a disadvantage to Rangers playing, no."
authors: Tyrone Smith - BBC Sport Scotland Senior Reporter

articles.title: Karl celebrates comeback and hopes to be included in Germany squad
articles.summary: Bayern Munich midfielder Lennart Karl celebrated his comeback from injury in the 5-1 win against VfB Stuttgart on Friday evening and now hopes quickly to fin...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich midfielder Lennart Karl celebrated his comeback from injury in the 5-1 win against VfB Stuttgart on Friday evening and now hopes quickly to find his way back to the Germany national team.

"I'm very happy to be back," he said after the Bundesliga opener.

"It was a very, very tough journey. At first, it was more of a mental challenge, and then it became more of a physical one. But the team supported me very well. The staff really helped me get through that tough time. That's definitely why I was able to come back strong."

Karl was included in Germany's World Cup squad by then-coach Julian Nagelsmann, but suffered a hamstring injury during training camp and was ruled him out of the tournament.

After the elimination in the round of 32, Nagelsmann stepped down from his position and former Liverpool coach Jürgen Klopp took charge of the team.

Karl said he hasn't spoken with Klopp yet, but that he hopes to be included in the squad the coach will name on September 17 for Nations League matches against the Netherlands, Greece and Serbia.

"I hope to be included. I'm working very hard to be completely fit again. We will see what the coach will do," Karl said.

articles.title: New York Giants 53-man projection: Final prediction before cutdown day
articles.summary: The preseason is over and cutdown day is around the bend, so here's a final New York Giants 53-man roster projection.
articles.body:
With the preseason now complete following Friday night's 23-6 victory over the Jets, the New York Giants ' roster hierarchy has grown clearer under head coach John Harbaugh.

Three exhibition games and a full summer of practices have sharpened evaluations across multiple position groups, prompting several notable adjustments from last week's projection as the picture comes into focus.

This final 53-man outlook accounts for the physical demands of camp, which continues through September 3, along with special-teams contributions, positional versatility, and standout performances in the last preseason contest. Harbaugh's preference for versatile, reliable contributors continues to shape the depth chart as the Sunday 6:00 p.m. ET deadline arrives and the Giants turn their attention to the September 13 opener against Dallas.

As anticipated, nothing changed here. The Giants were always going to go with Dart and Winston, and that remains the case. Allen played himself out of a job, so expect Haener to land on the practice squad.

There was a thought that Tyrone Tracy Jr. might have entered Friday night's game closer to the bubble. Still, he rebounded after two rough weeks and shined until exiting the game with a neck injury and concussion evaluation. Bankston may be the sneaky practice squad player here.

In : Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary, Najee Harris, and Patrick Ricard

Out: Eric Gray, Damon Bankston, Grant Finley

I've consistently had the Giants carrying seven wide receivers on their initial 53-man roster, but I no longer believe that will be the case. They lost Calvin Austin III to a torn ACL and Braxton Berrios was awful in his final dress rehearsal. OBJ gets in and Cambre steals a spot.

In : Malik Nabers, Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields, Odell Beckham Jr., Dalen Cambre

Out: Braxton Berrios, Isaiah Hodgins, Jalin Hyatt, Xavier Gipson, Kobe Prentice

Fidone came on at the end, but it's too little, too late. However, he is likely to end up on the practice squad and will potentially see some action later this season.

In : Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson, Chris Manhertz

Out: Tanner Conner, Thomas Fidone II, Josiah Deguara

Hudson did himself no favors with a mediocre performance on Friday, and now finds himself on the outside looking in. Patrick ultimately gets the backup job at center, although his injuries are something to keep an eye on. He dealt with a knee issue this summer and appeared to suffer a wrist/hand injury against the Jets.

In : Andrew Thomas, Jon Runyan Jr., John Michael Schmitz, Francis Mauigoa, Jermaine Eluemunor, Marcus Mbow, Aaron Stinnie, J.C. Davis, Lucas Patrick

Out: Bryan Hudson, Evan Neal, Jake Kubas, Ryan Schernecke, Jarrod Gray, Brenden Jaimes

Reader, Harris, and Colton are locks here. However, there are going to be some major changes to the team's depth along the defensive line over the next 48 hours. Outside of the top three, no one did enough to inspire any sort of confidence or trust. Jamison-Travis ultimately lands on the practice squad, while new faces will likely fill out the depth.

In : D.J. Reader, Shelby Harris, Chauncey Golston, Darius Alexander, Leki Fotu, Josh Tupou

Out: Bobby Jamison-Travis, Zacch Pickens, Marlon Davidson, Anquin Barnes Jr., Ben Barten

Many predict the Giants will only carry three edge rushers on the 53-man roster, but there is no denying that Ford has forced a difficult conversation. He played so well this preseason that a practice squad spot might get stolen away. I feel like he's earned it and gets one of the final 53-man roster spots.

In : Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Trace Ford

Barnes won his battle with Muasau outright on Friday night. His interception showed he can do a little something on defense if called upon, while also serving as a reliable special teams option. Muasau, who missed a huge opportunity on an 81-yard Jordan Stout punt, likely heads to the practice squad.

In : Tremaine Edmunds, Arvell Reese, Micah McFadden, Jack Kelly, Zaire Barnes

Out: Anfernee Orji, Darius Muasau, Chandler Martin

Black played well enough to be in the conversation for the final cornerback spot. A minor injury to Green -- one that won't keep him out "too long" -- may be the deciding factor. If "too long" means a few days, it won't matter. If it means a few weeks, Black gets the nod.

In : Paulson Adebo, Greg Newsome II, Dru Phillips, Deonte Banks, Colton Hood, Korie Black

The Giants probably toil around with the idea of carrying a fifth safety -- and perhaps they do after the initial wave of changes -- but the initial 53-man will only have four -- the obvious four.

In : Jevon Holland, Tyler Nubin, Ar'Darius Washington, Jason Pinnock

Out: Raheem Layne, Elijah Campbell, JT Woods, Ugochukwu Amadi, Beau Brade

The debate about the starting kicker was settled on Friday night when Harbaugh revealed that Zvada had won the job.

In : Dominic Zvada (K), Jordan Stout (P), Ben Mann (LS)

articles.title: 'Small steps' for Schmidt at Ulster - Best
articles.summary: Rory Best says Joe Schmidt's new role with Ulster is a case of "small steps" as the province seek to use the former Ireland coach's expertise to build a plat...
articles.body:
Rory Best says Joe Schmidt's new role with Ulster is a case of "small steps" as the province seek to use the former Ireland coach's expertise to build a platform for long-term success.

Schmidt was appointed Ulster's coach development adviser last month after ending his two-year stint as Australia boss, a newly created role focused on the province's coaching pathway.

The 60-year-old is one of Ireland's most successful coaches having led the national team to three Six Nations titles - including the 2018 Grand Slam - during a six-year spell and Leinster to two European Cups.

"I don't want to just be successful this season or in a year or two, it has to be a continuous process and to do that we need continuity of what's coming behind it and that's why Joe is here," said Ulster general manager Rory Best, who was appointed Ireland captain by Schmidt in 2016.

"Joe was the best coach I worked under as a head coach. Since then, he's went on, he's coached the All Blacks, Australia. He's across the New Zealand underage system, the Australian underage system, from his time in Leinster the Irish underage system.

"So to bring all the best practices together, ultimately what you want to do is to create a conveyor belt. The lift it gives everyone around the place is brilliant. We're delighted to have him.

"Obviously the next step is to get him head to toe in Ulster gear, but it's small steps."

Schmidt was present at an open training session for Ulster's senior men's team in Banbridge on Friday as Murphy's side ramp up preparations for the 2026-27 season.

Murphy - who worked alongside the Kiwi at Leinster and Ireland - said it was a "genius idea" by Best to get Schmidt involved.

"Myself and Joe go back a long time. Besty, I thought it was a genius idea bringing him over," he said.

"He's helping through the pathway and having a look at that area and making sure we have a supply of players to feed this Ulster senior team.

"He's here today to have a look at training and we'd be crazy not to use a person like that in relation in giving us a bit of feedback about how we go about our business."

Murphy is in the process of reintegrating Ulster's cohort of Ireland internationals back into training after their Nations Championship exertions in July.

A promising 2025-26 season ended in disappointing fashion for Ulster as they missed out on Investec Champions Cup qualification after finishing ninth in the United Rugby Championship and losing the Challenge Cup final to Montpellier.

Ulster face Edinburgh and Ospreys in pre-season friendlies before beginning their URC campaign against the former in Belfast on 25 September.

During a busy summer of squad additions and departures, Ulster signed the likes of forwards Eli Snyman, Ben Donnell and Keynan Knox and backs Chay Mullins, Matthew Devine and Jamie Benson, while losing key players such as Werner Kok and Angus Bell.

"I think our squad depth has improved, especially in key positions," said Murphy, who is entering his third full season in charge.

"Ben Donnell can play in back row and second row, Eli in the second row gives us more experience in that area. Two tight-heads knocking around in Keynan Knox and Eduardo Bello creates pressure and competition for places which is really positive.

"Tom O'Toole, Scotty Wilson and Tom McAllister were there last year, those lads have to fight it out now to get themselves on the pitch, which is great.

"Our two half-backs that have come in, Matty Devine and young Benson, they've both fitted in really well and upped the level of competition to get your name on the sheet, so that's been really positive."

articles.title: The Top 25 Michigan men’s basketball players since 1989: No. 1
articles.summary: The end of the offseason is here. Find out who takes our top spot of the best Michigan basketball players since 1989:
articles.body:
We've reached the end of the Michigan Wolverines' athletics offseason, and with that concludes our series ranking the top-25 players for the men's basketball team in between the 1989 and 2026 national championships. The celebration of Dusty May and this program winning their first national title in more than three decades concludes with the only National Player of the Year in this era and one of two in the history of the program — Trey Burke.

Chris Webber may have been the better basketball prospect. Juwan Howard had the longer Michigan career. Yaxel Lendeborg won a national championship and Big Ten Player of the Year.

But Burke reached a level of individual accolades none of those greats did in their careers. For one season, Burke was not merely the best player in Ann Arbor, he was the best player in college basketball. And unlike many others who have earned that crown, Burke backed it up with one of the most memorable NCAA Tournament runs in Michigan history.

Despite playing only two seasons in Ann Arbor, Burke finished with 1,231 points, 416 assists and 93 steals. His 416 assists ranked seventh in Michigan history when he left, despite playing just two seasons. In 73 career games, he accomplished what most players need four years to even approach.

It was even more pivotal because Burke was the face of the turning point of the John Beilein era, and he wasn't an elite prospect coming out of high school. Michigan needed a point guard after Darius Morris left for the NBA, and Burke did more than just fill his shoes. Burke averaged 14.8 points, 4.6 assists and 3.5 rebounds per game as a true freshman. He led the team in scoring, steals and assists, breaking a 27-year old freshman assist record in the process. That led to him winning Big Ten Freshman of the Year and seven Big Ten Freshman of the Week honors, and being named a second-team All-Big Ten, an AP All-American honorable mention.

Led by a freshman Burke, the Wolverines went 13-5 in the Big Ten, earning a share of the program's first Big Ten regular-season championship in 26 years. In the Big Ten Tournament opener, Burke exploded for a career-high 30 points in a 73-69 overtime win while shooting 11-for-14 from the field. A disappointing loss to Ohio State ended the Wolverines' tournament run, and then a stunning loss in the Round of 64 in the NCAA Tournament to Ohio could have spelled the end of his career.

Instead, Burke decided to return for one more season, in part because of the best freshman class Beilein brought in during his tenure. Nik Stauskas, Glenn Robinson III, Mitch McGary, Spike Albrecht and Caris LeVert all joined the team and played large roles alongside Burke and his counterpart Tim Hardaway Jr. It was the culmination of everything clicking at the right time and Burke was the focal point, ascending from Big Ten Freshman of the Year to National Player of the Year.

Michigan came into the 2012-13 season as the No. 5 team in the country and started 16-0. But the team played in a LOADED Big Ten — Ohio State, Michigan State, Indiana and Minnesota all ranked in the top-10, and the Wolverines had two top-five matchups with the Hoosiers. Still, the Wolverines earned the No. 1 ranking in the AP Poll for the first time since the Fab Five era in late January.

Despite the loaded conference, Burke was by far the best player. In Big Ten play, Burke averaged 20.2 points, 6.4 assists and two steals per game while shooting 40.4 percent from behind the arc. He scored at least 15 points in all 18 Big Ten games and broke Michigan's single-season assist record with 260 on a 3-to-1 turnover ratio. It was statistically one of the most efficient seasons a guard has had in program history.

Not only did Burke win Big Ten Player of the Year over the likes of Victor Oladipo, Cody Zeller and Aaron Craft from both the coaches and media, but he also swept the national awards. He earned the Wooden Award, Naismith Trophy, AP National Player of the Year, NABC Player of the Year, Oscar Robertson Trophy, SI's National Player of the Year, and the Bob Cousy Award. It wasn't just one organization, it was consensus that Burke was the best player in college basketball.

The NCAA Tournament run that coincided hung on Burke's shoulders. There's no better example than the Sweet 16 matchup with the AP's No. 3 team in the country, the Kansas Jayhawks. Michigan trailed by 14 in the second half and were still down double digits with seven minutes remaining. After not scoring in the first half, Burke took over. For the rest of the game, Burke scored 23 points and hit "The Trey" to tie the game and send it to overtime:

It capped a 23-8 run for the Wolverines over the final seven minutes, and Michigan won 87-85 in overtime.

Beilein's team road the momentum from that game into a National Championship appearance against the AP No. 2 team in the country, Louisville. It was a fantastic back-and-forth game, as Burke carried the Wolverines with 24 points.

The turning point was with 5:09 remaining. Louisville led 67-64 when Burke chased down Peyton Siva in transition and cleanly blocked the ball. However, it was called a foul by the officials in one of the most controversial calls in NCAA Tournament history:

Instead of Michigan riding the momentum from its best player making a championship play, the Cardinals extended their lead to two possessions and went on a 9-2 run that sealed the game.

Despite falling short, Burke led the resurrection of Michigan men's basketball. He wasn't just the face of college basketball, he helped Michigan win a Big Ten regular-season title, reach No. 1 in the polls, appear in the program's first Final Four in 20 years, and make their first National Championship appearance since the Fab Five era.

For the first time in what felt like eons, the Wolverines were back among college basketball's elite. Without Burke and this run, what we saw last season with Dusty May and crew wouldn't have happened. He trailblazed the path to a title and a made Ann Arbor a place for college basketball's best once again.

articles.title: Opponent Preview: Missouri Tigers
articles.summary: Next on our opponent preview is the Missouri Tigers, the sometimes forgotten child of the SEC. The Dawg and Tigers have an interesting history since Missouri...
articles.body:
Next on our opponent preview is the Missouri Tigers, the sometimes forgotten child of the SEC. The Dawg and Tigers have an interesting history since Missouri moved into the SEC. Things started with Missouri claiming Georgia played old man football, then Jarvis Jones reminding them it's actually grown man football.

Sadly, the Tigers beat Georgia in 2013 on the way to their only SEC Championship Game appearance. Also, let's not forget Jacob Eason to Isaiah McKenzie on fourth down to win it in 2016 (but let's forget the 9-6 Georgia win in 2015).

In 2026, we square off against Missouri again, with the Tigers ranked #25 in the preseason AP Poll.

The Missouri offense starts with running back Ahmad Hardy. A preseason first team all-SEC selection, Hardy is one of the best running backs in nation. He is their bell cow and is the engine to the offense. However, Hardy had an extremely frightening scare during the offseason. Hardy was shot in the leg in May and immediately underwent surgery. Head coach Eli Drinkwitz has said the Hardy is medically cleared but is still working his way back. He has already been ruled out for Missouri's opener, and here is hoping that Hardy is fully recovered and healthy, getting back to the field soon. Hardy will be running behind a good offensive line, anchored by preseason All-SEC first team selection Cayden Green.

While the running game gets the headlines, the quarterback position is a slight question mark. Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons will be under center for the Tigers this year. Simmons was suppose to be the Rebels' starting quarterback last season before getting Wally Pipped by Trinidad Chambliss. Simmons will look to play an entire season the same way he played in his one drive against Georgia in 2024 – very, very well. Hopefully the Dawgs defense has an answer for Simmons this time around.

The Missouri defense will feature several transfers, namely Robert Woodyard Jr. from Auburn. Woodyard Jr. was named a third team preseason third team all-SEC selection, and the linebacker will be looked at as one of the leaders on defense.

The Mizzou defensive line and pass rush will take a step back in 2016 after losing former Georgia pass rusher Damon Wilson to Miami. Darris Smith is the major returning impact player along the d-line, but the defense will need to find a few other impact players that includes four transfers.

The secondary will also feature several transfers after almost all impact players will be playing elsewhere. The theory to beating Missouri's defense will be through the air, as there are question marks about their secondary and pass rush.

Missouri will be a solid team in 2026, but they are not coming into Athens and leaving with a victory. It may be a higher scoring affair, but the Dawgs will prevail 44-24.

articles.title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 15 Days Remaining
articles.summary: We continue our countdown to the Panthers opening the 2026 season against the Chicago Bears
articles.body:
Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We've always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial.

Mike Rucker was an elite complementary defensive end. It might be a disservice to call him that, but that's kind of what he was simply due to the sheer talent alongside him for much of his time in Carolina.

The Panthers drafted Rucker in the second round of the 1999 NFL Draft. He played in a rotational role for his first two seasons and accumulated 5.5 sacks in that time. After the retirement of Reggie White, Rucker slid in to the starting defensive end spot opposite Jay Williams. He was the best pass rusher on the team that season, leading the group with nine sacks as the team struggled to a 1-15 record. That putrid season allowed the team to draft Julius Peppers, and he and Rucker formed one of the most formidable edge duos in the league with monsters on the interior like Kris Jenkins making the entire front four a nightmare for the rest of the league.

Rucker hit double digit sacks in each of his first two seasons opposite Peppers. His sack production dipped in the subsequent seasons, but he was still a very effective player as an edge setter and all around solid defensive end. He tore his ACL near the end of the 2006 season. He was able to rehab in time to return for the 2007 season, and despite quickly regaining his pre-injury form, he decided to call it a career after that season at the age of 33.

Rucker amassed 55.5 sacks in his time in Carolina, good for third in franchise history behind Peppers and Charles Johnson. He was also credited with two safeties, which is tied for the most in Panthers history. He never suited up for another team and has remained connected with the franchise and the city of Charlotte since his retirement; he called Panthers preseason games on local TV for a number of years. He's a Carolina Panther through and through, For that, and for his time and effectiveness on the field as a Panther, he earns spot number 15 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

articles.title: Golden Tempo vs. Renegade rematch highlights 157th running of Travers Stakes
articles.summary: Golden Tempo's chance for Saratoga immortality has arrived. To achieve it, he'll have to get past his most persistent rival and a host of other talented cont...
articles.body:
SARATOGA SPRINGS - Golden Tempo 's chance for Saratoga immortality has arrived. To achieve it, he'll have to get past his most persistent rival and a host of other talented contenders.

Trained by Cherie DeVaux, Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes winner Golden Tempo is the morning-line favorite for the 157th running of the Travers Stakes on Saturday at Saratoga Race Course. The Grade 1, $1.25 million race is set for a 6:35 p.m. post time as part of a blockbuster 14-race card.

For Golden Tempo, the 1 ¼-mile Travers will mark his first start since June 6, when he copied his Kentucky Derby formula by going last-to-first to win the final Belmont of the Triple Crown race's three-year residency in Saratoga.

"He is so classy, he is so professional. He's been like that his entire life," DeVaux told the New York Racing Association. "He's a horse who just continues to improve and continues to mature and change. … That's why each race we're hoping he's going to continue to improve, which he has done so far."

Golden Tempo, who drew the No. 9 post in the 10-horse Travers field, will be ridden once again by Saratoga's leading jockey, Jose Ortiz, who piloted him to victories in two-thirds of this year's Triple Crown.

Though an illness in June disrupted Golden Tempo's training schedule at DeVaux's Keeneland barn and kept him out of a planned prep earlier in this month in the Jim Dandy, it's all systems go as the colt attempts to follow Sovereignty's path from 2025 in winning the Derby, Belmont and Travers.

Four of the last five Belmont winners to enter the Travers have gone on to win it, but Saratoga's biggest race has been a bit less forgiving to Kentucky Derby winners. When Sovereignty won last year's Midsummer Derby, he became the first horse who won the Run for the Roses to win the Travers since Street Sense in 2007.

"He looks very good," Ortiz told the Times Union earlier this week. "We're very happy with him."

Golden Tempo's biggest rival in the Travers? That's Renegade, the horse he ran down to beat by a neck in the Kentucky Derby.

"I'm 0-for-12 in the Derby, but I never lost by a neck," said Mike Repole, who co-owns Renegade with Robert and Lawana Low.

Trained by Todd Pletcher, Renegade went on to finish third behind Golden Tempo and Commandment in the Belmont, then bounced back with a win in the Jim Dandy on Aug. 1.

All three of Pletcher's previous Travers winners won the race coming off a Jim Dandy victory. Two of those horses, 2011 winner Stay Thirsty and 2024 winner Fierceness, were owned by Repole.

"He's pretty uncomplicated," Pletcher told NYRA. "He's been able to do it in all kinds of scenarios, so we're not looking to change anything. He's been in peak form the past couple of weeks and he acts to me like he's sitting on a big race."

"I have great respect for Renegade. I feel like they are all rivals when you are the favorite. Everybody is out to get you, so I think it will be interesting," said DeVaux.

With his regular rider Irad Ortiz Jr. out with an injury, Tyler Gaffalione will inherit the mount on Renegade in the Travers.

"Tyler's a great rider," Repole said. "We've ridden him before. He's in Kentucky a little too much for us to be able to ride him more often, but we're excited. He's a class A jockey and we know he's going to give him a great ride."

If there's a disruption to the Golden Tempo-Renegade showdown, it could come in the form of Napoleon Solo. The Chad Summers-trained colt won the Preakness when neither Golden Tempo nor Renegade was in the field, and is coming off a second-place finish in the Haskell over a sloppy Monmouth Park track.

"This is the deepest Travers we've seen in a long time," Summers said. "Obviously, Golden Tempo is the favorite for the 3-year-old championship, but he's never run against us before. So, we'll see what happens in the race."

Two lightly-raced colts from powerhouse barns could also complicate proceedings.

Leading Change, trained by Brad Cox, has only raced twice in his career, but is coming off a win in the Grade 3 Indiana Derby on July 11. Then there's Sea Strike, trained by Chad Brown, who scored an 8 ¼-length win in the Curlin at Saratoga on the day after the Jim Dandy while making just his third career start.

"He is a lightly-raced horse and we'll see if we can get another eighth of a mile out of him at the mile and a quarter and see how he does," said Brown, a Mechanicville native who also has Emerging Market in the Travers field. "On figures, it looks like he fits."

Rounding out the Travers field are Baby Vino, who won the Haskell at 28-1 odds in his last start; The Puma, the Haskell's fourth-place finisher; Ocelli, who finished third in the Derby and fourth in the Preakness but is winless in 10 career starts; and Silent Tactic, who was a strong third in the Jim Dandy while making his first start in more than four months.

Whether one of the new contenders emerges or if it falls back into another Golden Tempo vs. Renegade duel won't be determined until the Travers leaves the gate.

"I have always said this race is a bit different than the other races because horses do a lot of maturing throughout the summer, colts especially, so it will be interesting to see how they both perform," DeVaux said. "And we have new horses in the race, too, and they weren't part of the conversation during Belmont week."

Emerging Market (Chad Brown, Ricardo Santana Jr., 15-1)

Leading Change (Brad Cox, Manny Franco, 12-1)

Napoleon Solo (Chad Summers, John Velazquez, 8-1)

The Puma (Gustavo Delgado, Javier Castellano, 8-1)

Renegade (Todd Pletcher, Tyler Gaffalione, 3-1)

Ocelli (Whit Beckman, Edgar Zayas, 20-1)

Sea Strike (Chad Brown, Flavien Prat, 5-1)

Baby Vino (Lindsay Schultz, Paco Lopez, 10-1)

Golden Tempo (Cherie DeVaux, Jose Ortiz, 5-2)

Silent Tactic (Mark Casse, Luis Saez, 10-1)

*Trainer, jockey, morning-line odds in parentheses

articles.title: 5 Broncos’ players who made a good case for a roster spot in final preseason game
articles.summary: Here are five players that may have made a good case for a roster spot with the Denver Broncos after their performance in the final preseason game.
articles.body:
The final preseason game was anything but boring as the Denver Broncos rolled over the Minnesota Vikings in a 34-6 blowout win . There were a lot of great individual performances last night and head coach Sean Payton is going to have a real problem filling out the back end of the initial 53-man roster and deciding who he might be able to sneak onto the 16-man practice squad.

Out of all those performances, here are four players we think made a really good case for an active roster spot after that final preseason game.

Cody Schrader absolutely killed it and showed just a ton of talent at the running back position. He can run, he can catch, and he can block out of the backfield. He had over 100 yards from scrimmage, including a touchdown in the back of the end zone on a broken play. I honestly think he might cost Jaleel McLaughlin his spot on the roster with this performance. – Sadaraine

Red Murdock actually had a fairly quiet night on the tackle side of things with just four total tackles, but he had a critical forced fumble living up to his turnover creating reputation. I feel like both he and Taurean York are playmakers, but its also hard to see two rookies getting two active roster spots. I feel like one of them will get it and the other gets stowed away on the practice squad, but we might be seeing the future unfold at inside linebacker with these two. – Tim Lynch

Sam Ehlinger had a really good showing against the Vikings. Carrying a 3rd QB might not be what Sean Payton wants to do, but Ehlinger showed that he can hold down a spot on a roster. 15/20 for 233 yards and 3 TDs. I don't care who it was against. His performance was worthy of note. He might not find himself on the final roster, but you can bet that the Broncos want to keep him around, while other teams might be interested in giving him a shot at a true backup spot. – Adam Malnati

Justin Joly didn't stand out much in the first two preseason games, but his 88-yard touchdown pass from Sam Ehlinger in the fourth quarter versus the Minnesota Vikings was incredible. This solidified his spot as one of the depth tight ends on the roster. Moreover, it was emblematic of the big-time plays he made throughout college. Hopefully this is just the first of many touchdowns he scores in his career with the Broncos. – Chris Hart

This kid just kept making plays in the return game. He added a second 40+ yard kick return last night with a 48-yard kick return, but more importantly, he adjusted field position in each of his two punt returns also with 2 returns for 31 yards. If it wasn't for the presence of Marvin Mims Jr., I think he would make the final 53-man roster. However, Denver might have found the heir of Mims if he isn't extended by free agency next March. We'll have to see if they can hide Katsis away on the practice squad. – Tim Lynch

articles.title: Phillies news: Jesus Luzardo, Andrew Painter, George Lombard, Jr.
articles.summary: MLB needs to keep teams where they are
articles.body:
I think it's great that the Rays are going to stay in Tampa Bay. I hate seeing teams relocate franchises regardless of the sport, so seeing that they are basically at the finish line to build a new stadium is good for Major League Baseball.

Jesus Luzardo has been fantastic this year, perhaps a little under the radar. How he is making hitters look is just plain silly ($).

The front office times, they are a'changin'. The team announced a slew of moves to the front office, including one that admits player development is a problem.

Andrew Painter has gotten his fastball to a better place. It's not great yet, but he talks about how he has put the work in ($).

Legalized gambling has taken its toll on some of the players in the game. This is a fascinating story that is also kind of sad ($).

Tampa Bay has decided to give the Rays a little over $2 billion to build a new stadium, a pretty large step in actually getting that stadium built.

George Lombard, Jr. was supposed to be a solid defensive shortstop for the Yankees upon promotion. Now he has a six-game error streak.

articles.title: Newcastle Makes Major Nick Woltemade Decision as Transfer Rumors Grow: Report
articles.summary: Newcastle United’s attempts to reshape its attack have placed Nick Woltemade’s future under increasing scrutiny, with several reports over the past few days...
articles.body:
Newcastle United's attempts to reshape its attack have placed Nick Woltemade's future under increasing scrutiny, with several reports over the past few days pointing toward a possible departure before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

That uncertainty might have taken its most significant step forward in the last few hours, as talkSPORT reported on Friday that Newcastle is "actively seeking to offload" the Germany international.

According to talkSPORT, the Magpies are no longer simply prepared to consider approaches from outside, but are actively looking for a solution and pitching the player to other clubs only 12 months after making Woltemade its club-record signing.

"Newcastle are actively seeking to offload Nick Woltemade before the transfer window shuts, talkSPORT understands," the report says. "It now appears that Woltemade is not part of the long-term plans at St James' Park, with Newcastle keen to move him on. The Germany international may already have options to consider, with Napoli reportedly among those keen."

The development follows a difficult first season for Woltemade on Tyneside after he arrived for a massive £69 million (€80 million) fee from Stuttgart. Woltemade started the season impressively but ultimately only scored 11 goals across 51 appearances, including eight in the Premier League, with his production dropping dramatically as the year progressed.

New manager and fellow German Matthias Jaissle initially appeared prepared to offer his compatriot another opportunity, but Woltemade was an unused substitute in Newcastle's 2-2 league draw against Liverpool. He then started Wednesday's 3-2 Carabao Cup victory over West Brom without scoring.

Making Newcastle's job easier at finding Woltemade a new home is that there already is substantial interest in the Germany international.

Fabrizio Romano reported Thursday that Napoli had contacted Newcastle during the previous 24 hours to ask about Woltemade's availability on loan.

TEAMtalk's Graeme Bailey, meanwhile, reported that intermediaries held discussions with Stuttgart regarding a possible return to his former club, while Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig have also shown interest.

The Athletic's Chris Waugh reported that Newcastle would risk negatively affecting its UEFA financial position by accepting a substantial permanent loss on Woltemade, making a temporary departure on loan more likely if he leaves this summer.

Newcastle's incoming business could still determine whether anything happens, as the Magpies are pursuing at least one more attacker, with Lille's Matias Fernandez-Pardo the No. 1 target and Stuttgart's Bilal El Khannouss his preferred alternative .

Should Newcastle cut its losses on Woltemade now, or would a loan be the smarter way to protect its £69 million investment? Let us know in the comments below.

Boston College will attempt to get back on track in the third year of the Bill O'Brien era.

After appearing in the Pinstripe Bowl and finishing with a 7-6 record in 2024, the Eagles struggled last year, dropping 10 straight games in the middle of the season to eliminate any chance of another bowl berth.

Now, the pressure is on O'Brien with Boston College increasing its financial investment in the football program. Can the Eagles start the new campaign on a high note with a victory against Cincinnati in their 2026 season opener?
